'''Roeland Johannes Maria Nolte''' (16 December 1944 – 15 February 2024) was a Dutch chemist, known for his work in the fields of [[organic chemistry]], [[biochemistry]], [[polymer chemistry]], and [[supramolecular chemistry]]. He was an emeritus [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] professor<ref name="lifea">{{Cite web|url=https://www.volkskrant.nl/archief/akademie-benoemt-superprofessoren~a744139/|title=Akademie benoemt superprofessoren, Volkskrant, 31 mei 2003|website=de Volkskrant}}</ref><ref name="lifeb">{{Cite web|url=http://www.liesbethkoenen.nl/archief/mini-mini-machientjes-bouwen-met-moleculen/|title="Minimachientjes bouwen met moleculen", Interview with Roeland Nolte by Liesbeth Koenen, Akademie Nieuws, October 2003"|website=www.liesbethkoenen.nl}}</ref> and an emeritus professor of organic chemistry at [[Radboud University]] in [[Nijmegen]], The Netherlands. Until his death, he held a special chair, i.e. professor of [[molecular nanotechnology]], at Radboud University. Nolte was considered to be one of the pioneers of the field of supramolecular chemistry, which encompasses the design and synthesis of new [[chemical structure]]s from low molecular weight compounds and [[biopolymer]]s using [[non-covalent interaction]]s. He published many studies on [[supramolecular assembly]] and biomimetic catalysts, which find applications in the field of [[nanomaterials]] and [[medicine]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|last=Mosher|first=Dave|date=27 February 2012|title=Video: First Nanorockets Might Shuttle Drugs, Robo-Surgeons|magazine=Wired |url=https://www.wired.com/2012/02/nanoscopic-rocket-engines/|via=www.wired.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last1=Blankesteijn |first1=HB Herbert |title=Herbert Blankesteijn, Katalyserende knijpers en moleculaire vazen, NRC, 17 maart 1994|work=NRC |date=17 March 1994 |url=https://www.nrc.nl/nieuws/1994/03/17/katalyserende-knijpers-en-moleculaire-vazen-7217719-a971050//}}</ref><ref name="refer5">{{Cite web|title='Voorlopig zie ik nog geen kans' &#124; C2W|url=https://www.c2w.nl/nieuws/voorlopig-zie-ik-nog-geen-kans|website=www.c2w.nl}}</ref>

==Education==
Nolte attended Gymnasium Ruimzicht in [[Doetinchem]], where he graduated in 1963. Thereafter, he studied [[chemistry]] at the [[University of Utrecht]], where he received his master's degree in 1969.<ref name="cv123">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Nolte_Roeland|title=Academy of Europe: Nolte Roeland|website=www.ae-info.org}}</ref> He continued his studies at the same university, earning a Ph.D. in [[physical organic chemistry]] on the synthesis and properties of a new type of [[polymer]] in 1973 (supervisor Wiendelt Drenth).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/227622351|title=Roeland J.M. Nolte, Synthese en isomerisatie van polyisocyaniden (Synthesis and isomerization of polyisocyanides), thesis Utrecht 1973}}</ref> After a postdoctoral stage with Nobel laureate [[Donald J. Cram]] at [[UCLA]], he joined the Faculty of Science of Utrecht University as an assistant professor.<ref name="cv123"/><ref>[https://www.ru.nl/en/about-us/news/in-memoriam-prof-roeland-jm-nolte In Memoriam Prof. Roeland J.M. Nolte]</ref>

==Career==
Nolte started his career as an assistant professor at the University of Utrecht and was promoted to associate professor in 1979.<ref name="cv123"/> In 1987, he moved to [[Radboud University]] in [[Nijmegen]] as a full professor of [[organic chemistry]].<ref name="cv123"/> Nolte was appointed adjunct professor of [[supramolecular chemistry]] at the [[Eindhoven University of Technology]] in 1994.<ref name="cv123"/> In 2002, he became the first director of the new Institute for Molecules and Materials at Radboud University in Nijmegen, which he remained until his retirement in 2010.<ref name="cv123"/> In honour of his contributions to science, he was awarded a special [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]] Professorship in 2003.<ref name="lifea"/><ref name="lifeb"/> Nolte retired in 2010, after which he received a special university professorship in [[molecular nanotechnology]] at Radboud University.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.voxweb.nl/vox-magazine/VOX07-jg10-totaal-1.pdf|title=Retirement interview with Roeland Nolte}}</ref>

==Work==
Nolte's research focused on supramolecular systems with special properties and functions. These are designed based on the principles of organic chemistry and [[polymer chemistry]], usually by first synthesizing [[molecular building blocks]] of different shapes and properties, which are subsequently self-assembled in a second step to form functional [[nanostructure]]s.<ref name="lifeb"/><ref name="new 9">{{Cite web|url=https://www.vpro.nl/speel~WO_VPRO_036206~hoe-zo-wetenschapcafé-06-05-2011-moleculaire-bouwdoos~.html|title=Roeland Nolte explains the philosophy of his work. Video recording of interview on May 6, 2011|date=23 May 2016 }}</ref> Self-assembly takes place by a combination of weak (supramolecular) interactions, such as [[hydrogen bonding]], [[Stacking (chemistry)|pi-pi-stacking]] interactions, [[van der Waals interaction]]s, and [[coordination bond]]s.<ref name="refer5"/> The designed structures find applications in the fields of [[materials science]] and [[catalysis]]. Nature was often used as a source of inspiration.

Very early on in his career, Nolte discovered the first example of a polymer with a stable helical structure, called an atropisomeric polymer, i.e. a polymer which cannot rotate around its main chain [[carbon]] atoms.<ref name="newr10">{{Cite book|url=https://doi.org/10.1002/9783527652532|title= G. Nenajdenko (24-8-2012) "Isocyanide Chemistry: Applications in Synthesis and Material Science", Chapter 16 Polyisocyanides, Wiley-VCH Verlag GmbH & Co. KGaA, Doi:10.1002/9783527652532|year= 2012|doi= 10.1002/9783527652532|isbn= 9783527652532|editor1-last= Nenajdenko|editor1-first= Valentine G}}</ref> He separated the left-handed and right-handed polymer helices and studied the mechanism of their formation, which was catalyzed by [[nickel]] ions and found to take place via a new mechanism, i.e. a [[polymerization]] reaction that takes place in a circular fashion around the metal center (merry-go-round mechanism).<ref name="newr10"/> Later studies on atropisomeric polymers derived from isocyanopeptides revealed that these compounds formed [[superhelical structure]]s by a supramolecular process of hierarchical self-assembly.<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1062224|title=This Week in Science: "Building β-Helical Polymers" |year=2001 |doi=10.1126/science.1062224 |pmid=11474106 |last1=Cornelissen |first1=J. J. |last2=Donners |first2=J. J. |last3=De Gelder |first3=R. |last4=Graswinckel |first4=W. S. |last5=Metselaar |first5=G. A. |last6=Rowan |first6=A. E. |last7=Sommerdijk |first7=N. A. |last8=Nolte |first8=R. J. |journal=Science |volume=293 |issue=5530 |pages=676–680 |s2cid=27109401 |url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title=beta -Helical polymers from isocyanopeptides|year=2001|pmid=11474106|last1=Cornelissen|first1=J. J.|last2=Donners|first2=J. J.|last3=De Gelder|first3=R.|last4=Graswinckel|first4=W. S.|last5=Metselaar|first5=G. A.|last6=Rowan|first6=A. E.|last7=Sommerdijk|first7=N. A.|last8=Nolte|first8=R. J.|journal=Science|volume=293|issue=5530|pages=676–80|doi=10.1126/science.1062224|s2cid=27109401}}</ref>

Other polyisocyanide derivatives formed [[hydrogel]]s at very low concentrations, displaying strain stiffening, i.e. they become stronger when a force is applied, a property that previously had only been found in [[natural material]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal|title= Materials science: Synthetic polymers with biological rigidity|year= 2013|pmid= 23354043|last1= Gardel|first1= M. L.|journal= Nature|volume= 493|issue= 7434|pages= 618–9|doi= 10.1038/nature11855|bibcode= 2013Natur.493..618G|s2cid= 38794910|doi-access= free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title= Responsive biomimetic networks from polyisocyanopeptide hydrogels|year= 2013|pmid= 23354048|last1= Kouwer|first1= P. H.|last7= Woltinge|first7= T.|last8= Schwartz|first8= E.|last9= Kitto|first9= H. J.|last10= Hoogenboom|first10= R.|last11= Picken|first11= S. J.|last12= Nolte|first12= R. Nolte pioneered the assembly of disc-like molecules, such as [[porphyrin]]s and [[phthalocyanine]]s into long [[supramolecular polymer]]s. Some of these formed superhelical structures by a process in which information is transferred stepwise from the building blocks to the [[polymer chain]]s and subsequently to the helical assembly of polymers.<ref>{{Cite journal|url= https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.284.5415.785|title= This week in Science: "Tuning Chirality"|year= 1999|doi= 10.1126/science.284.5415.785|pmid= 10221906|last1= Engelkamp|first1= H.|last2= Middelbeek|first2= S.|last3= Nolte|first3= R. J.|journal= Science|volume= 284|issue= 5415|pages= 785–8|doi= 10.1126/science.284.5415.785}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nrc.nl/|title= NRC Handelsblad 1-5-1999, Rob van den Berg "Tale of two twists" ("Vanzelf haargel. Moleculen vormen spontaan kubussen en wenteltrappen"}}</ref> These discs could also be used to generate layers for the alignment of liquid-crystalline molecules by a process of [[molecular self-assembly|self-assembly]] and aided assembly.<ref>{{Cite journal|journal= Science |url= https://www.science.org/doi/abs/10.1126/science.2006.314.5804.twis|title= This Week in Science: "Lining Up at the Front", Discussion of paper by R. van Hameren et al|date= December 2006|volume= 314|issue= 5804|pages= 1349|doi= 10.1126/science.2006.314.5804.twis|s2cid= 242264525|url-access= subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title= Macroscopic hierarchical surface patterning of porphyrin trimers via self-assembly and dewetting|year= 2006|pmid= 17138897|last1= Van Hameren|first1= R.|last2= Schön|first2= P.|last3= Van Buul|first3= A. Other research activities by Nolte involved the chemical modification of [[virus]]es, for which he coined the name chemical virology.<ref name="newr21">{{Cite journal|title= Self-assembly and optically triggered disassembly of hierarchical dendron-virus complexes|year= 2010|pmid= 20414241|last1= Kostiainen|first1= M. J.|journal= Nature Chemistry|volume= 2|issue= 5|pages= 394–9|doi= 10.1038/nchem.592|bibcode= 2010NatCh...2..394K}}</ref> In these viruses he encapsulated [[enzyme]]s, allowing him to study their activities in a confined environment by single molecule techniques.<ref>{{Cite journal|title= A virus-based single-enzyme nanoreactor|year= 2007|pmid= 18654389|last1= Comellas-Aragonès|first1= M.|last2= Engelkamp|first2= H.|last3= Claessen|first3= V. J.|last10= Nolte|first10= R. J.|last2= Scrimin|first2= P.|journal= Nature Chemistry|volume= 5|issue= 11|pages= 899–900|doi= 10.1038/nchem.1785|bibcode= 2013NatCh...5..899P}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|title= A clamp-like biohybrid catalyst for DNA oxidation|year= 2013|pmid= 24153373|last1= Van Dongen|first1= S. F.|last2= Clerx|first2= J.|last3= Nørgaard|first3= K.|last4= Bloemberg|first4= T. G.|last5= Cornelissen|first5= J. J.|last6= Trakselis|first6= M. A.|last7= Nelson|first7= S. W.|last8= Benkovic|first8= S. J.|last9= Rowan|first9= A. E.|last10= Nolte|first10= R. J.|journal= Nature Chemistry|volume= 5|issue= 11|pages= 945–51|doi= 10.1038/nchem.1752|bibcode= 2013NatCh...5..945V|hdl= 2066/117355|hdl-access= free}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.alphagalileo.org/en-gb/Item-Display/ItemId/103666|title= Chemists slide a splitting catalyst over DNA for the first time|date= 22 February 2024}}</ref> He also designed [[molecular machine]]s that can encode digital information into single polymer chains in the form of [[chirality (chemistry)|chiral]] [[chemical group]]s.<ref name="lifeb"/><ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.demorgen.be/tag/roeland-nolte|title= "Alle data van de wereld op een draadje plastic", Trouw, Februari 10, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.nemokennislink.nl/publicaties/het-is-mijn-droom-een-moleculaire-computer-in-elkaar-te-zetten/|title= It is my dream to construct a molecular computer, interview with Roeland Nolte by Mariska van Sprundel|date= 22 February 2024}}</ref>

==Death==
Nolte died in [[Nijmegen]] on 15 February 2024, at the age of 79.<ref>{{cite news |title=Overlijden KNCV-erelid Roeland Nolte |url=https://www.kncv.nl/k/n1110/news/view/209179/878/overlijden-kncv-erelid-roeland-nolte.html |access-date=17 February 2024 |publisher=KNCV |date=16 February 2024}}</ref>

==Awards==
Nolte received numerous lecture awards,<ref name="newr 28">{{Cite web|url= https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Nolte_Roeland|title= Information on cv of Roeland Nolte}}</ref> such as the Cornforth lectureship at the [[University of Sydney]],<ref name="newr 28"/> the Eli-Burnstein lectureship at the [[University of Pennsylvania]],<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.lrsm.upenn.edu/events/past-series-lectures/|title= Past Burstein and Maddin Series Lectures, The Laboratory for Research on the Structure of Matter, University of Pennsylvania}}</ref> and the Merck-Carl Pfister visiting professorship at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{Cite web|last1= Swager|first1= Timothy M.|url= http://web.mit.edu/annualreports/pres07/07.03.pdf|title= MIT Annual report 2006-2007|date= 30 June 2007}}</ref> He won several prizes, including the first Royal Academy of Science Professorship (2003),<ref name="lifea"/> the [[Izatt-Christensen Award]] (2006) for his studies on macrocyclic and supramolecular chemistry,<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.chem.byu.edu/faculty-and-staff/resources/international-symposium-on-macrocyclic-and-supramolecular-chemistry/awards/izatt-christensen-award-recipients/|title= Izatt Christensen award to Roeland Nolte}}</ref> and the Linstead Life-time Achievement Award for his pioneering work on supramolecular phthalocyanine systems.<ref>{{Cite web|url=  http://www.icpp-spp.org/icpp10/general/awards.php|title= Linstead Award to Roeland Nolte}}</ref> In 2006 he was elected a member of the [[Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/leden/nolte |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809130637/https://www.knaw.nl/leden/nolte |title=Roeland Nolte |language=nl |publisher=Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences |date= |archive-date=9 August 2022}}</ref> He was member of the [[Royal Belgian Academy of Sciences]],<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.kvab.be/nl/leden|title= Koninklijke Vlaamse Academie van Belgie voor Wetenschappen en Kunsten, Roeland Nolte}}</ref> and the [[Academia Europaea]].<ref name="cv123"/> He was furthermore awarded an Honorary Fellowship of the [[Royal Netherlands Chemical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://en.kncv.nl/kncv/honorary-members|title= Honorary members Royal Netherlands Chemical Society}}</ref> In 2004 he became a Knight in the [[Order of the Dutch Lion]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. dr. Roeland J.M. Nolte |work=Molecular Nanotechnology |url=https://www.ru.nl/science/molecularnanotechnology/people/members/prof-dr-roeland-n/ |publisher=Radboud University |access-date=22 February 2024}}</ref> After his retirement, he twice received a prestigious [[ERC Advanced Grant]] to study the encoding of information into polymers by supramolecular catalytic machines.<ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.ru.nl/deutsch/@1089904/roeland-nolte-erc-advanced-grant|title= Chemist Roeland Nolte receives his second ERC Advanced grant}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.voxweb.nl/nieuws/het-geheim-van-een-geleerde-op-leeftijd|title= roeland-nolte nieuws/|date= 31 March 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.knaw.nl/nl/actueel/nieuws/erc-advanced-grants-bij-knaw|title= ERC Advanced Grants for six KNAW members}}</ref>
